title: Ultrasound-guided lymph node fine-needle aspiration for evaluating post-vaccination germinal center responses in humans
protocol: Position the ultrasound probe for optimal visualization over an enlarged axillary lymph node recently receiving immunization.

Apply negative pressure to the syringe by withdrawing plunger to approximately the 2–3 mL mark on the syringe barrel using a gentle “to” and “fro” motion once puncture of the lymph node is visualized on US.
Enter the cortex of an axillary lymph node with a 23-gauge needle, guided by ultrasound visualization.
Repeat the aspiration process up to 4 times to gather sufficient sampling material.
Thoroughly flush the syringe barrel several times into 50 mL conical tubes using R10 media to remove cells adhering to the plastic.
Transport R10 media for US-LN-FNA in an Insulated Bio Transport Container.
Place the consented study participant into a supine position, with the arm of the targeted side raised above the head and resting on a pillow.
Scan the axilla by ultrasound (US) to identify potential lymph nodes for aspiration.
Confirm normal vascularity within a lymph node hilum using Color Doppler.
Identify potential vascular structures to be avoided during the FNA procedure.
Place a sterile drape on the study participant’s chest distal to the axilla to keep the US transducer sterile.
Prepare the axilla by swabbing generously with chlorhexidine, betadine, or a similar skin disinfectant solution.
Confirm that the participant is not allergic to any disinfectant solutions before they are applied to their skin.
Place a sterile cover over the ultrasound transducer before starting the fine needle aspiration procedure.
Administer local anesthesia by infiltrating the axillary skin and subcutaneous tissue with 2–4 mL of 1% lidocaine.
Introduce the lumbar puncture needle with attached syringe into the lymph node under direct ultrasound guidance.
Apply negative pressure to the syringe plunger to approximately the 2–3 mL mark on the syringe barrel once the needle tip is visualized within the lymph node.
Sample the lymph node cortex by withdrawing the needle slightly and redirecting it using a gentle “to and fro” motion.
Perform mild rotations and movements of the needle within the lymph node cortex while aspiration is being performed.
Withdraw the needle and syringe from the lymph node maintaining negative pressure on the syringe.
Remove the needle from the syringe barrel.
Flush the needle with fresh R10 media multiple times.
Submerge the tip of the needle into the 50 mL conical tube of R10 media labeled “For Collection”.
Carefully expel all contents of the needle and syringe into the media.
Withdraw 2–3 mL of R10 media from the tube labeled “For Flushing” into the unattached syringe.
Reattach the needle to the syringe.
Expel the media through the needle into the 50 mL conical tube labeled “For Collection”.
Remove the needle from the syringe barrel again.
Aspirate 2–3 mL of R10 media from the “For Flushing” tube into the syringe barrel.
Reattach the needle to the syringe.
Expel the media through the needle into the “For Collection” tube.

Repeat steps with another flush: remove the needle, aspirate media from the “For Flushing” tube into the syringe barrel, reattach the needle, and expel the media into the 50 mL conical tube labeled “For Collection” for a total of three flushes.
Discard the used lumbar needle and syringe in a biohazard sharps container.
Repeat steps “2.h” through “2.t” for a maximum of 4 passes or as much as tolerated by the study participant.
Use a new spinal needle for each pass.
Use a new syringe for each pass.
Repeat steps “2.p” through “2.s” until three flushes are completed for each of the four passes.
Replace the screw cap onto both “For Collection” and “For Flushing” 50 mL conical tubes after all passes are complete.
Place the capped tubes on wet ice in the screw-top cylindrical specimen container.
Inform the biospecimen processing operator if there is any doubt about which tube contains the sample.
Do not discard the “For Flushing” tube; send both tubes to the processing laboratory.
Place the screw-top cylindrical Saf-T-Pak specimen receptacle into an Insulated Bio Transport Container and transport the specimen over to the processing site.
Keep samples on ice until they are processed.
Wipe off any remaining ultrasound jelly from the study participant’s skin after sampling is complete.
Exert pressure with gauze if there is any bleeding from the skin puncture site(s) until the bleeding stops.
Apply an adhesive bandage to the skin.
Pre-cool the centrifuge at 4°C for processing aspirate.
Maintain temperature fluctuations between 2°C to 8°C throughout the whole process.
Centrifuge aspirate in the 50 mL tube labeled “For Collection” at 325 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Look for signs of sample collection in both tubes if indicated by the clinical team (darker reddish color and small pellet).
Check for a small red pellet after centrifugation.
Gently aspirate supernatant down to 10 mL using a serological pipette.
Aspirate remaining supernatant using a 1000 μL single channel pipette without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C).
Wash cells by bringing the volume to 50 mL with cold 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C).
Centrifuge sample at 325 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
After centrifugation, gently aspirate supernatant using methods previously described.
Visually estimate the pellet size.
Resuspend the potential pellet in 1 mL of 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C) if a pellet cannot be visualized.
Incubate the resuspended sample at ambient temperature for 4 minutes with gentle agitation.
Bring volume to 35 mL with cold 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C).
Centrifuge the sample at 325 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Proceed with a second RBC lysis if significant redness is observed in the pellet.
Gently aspirate supernatant and re-suspend the pellet in exactly 2 mL of cold 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C).
Transfer 20 μL of the cell suspension into a microcentrifuge tube containing 180 μL of 1× sterile PBS to create a 1:10 dilution.
Pipette up and down to mix thoroughly.
Add 20 μL of acridine orange and propidium iodide (AOPI) cell viability dye to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer 20 μL of the 1:10 diluted cell suspension to the tube containing AOPI.
Mix thoroughly (final dilution of 1:20).
Transfer 20 μL of the GCC/AOPI mix to one side of a labeled cell counter slide.
Use the Immune cells, low RBC assay on the Cellometer Auto 2000 to determine the cell concentration.
Prepare a live-dead cell staining solution for automated cell counting.
Use an automated system to determine cell count and viability by excluding platelets and red blood cells.
Ensure cell concentrations are within 1.0 × 10^5 − 1.0 × 10^7 for optimal counting accuracy.
If concentrations fall outside the recommended range, adjust the sample as necessary.
Consider using an equivalent automated cell counter if the Cellometer Auto 2000 is unavailable.
In absence of an automated system, perform viability analysis with a hemocytometer and trypan blue dye.
Do not use dyes that only determine total cell count, such as Turk’s Solution.
After counting cells, adjust the volume to 35 mL using cold 1× sterile PBS (2°C–8°C).
Centrifuge the tube containing the cells for 10 minutes at 325 × g and 4°C.
Observe and aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation to visualize the cell pellet.
Resuspend the sample in CFM if the pellet is not clearly visible despite low cell concentration.
Resuspend the cell pellet with CFM to achieve a concentration of 4000 cells/μL (4.0 × 10^6 cells/mL).
Denote aliquot as “partial” if remaining re-suspended cell suspension is between 0.5–1.0 mL and write the volume and number of total cells on the vial label.
Re-suspend with 500 μL (0.5 mL) CFM if fewer than 500 μL are required to achieve the necessary concentration, and record this information.
Transfer cell suspension into cryovials in 1 mL aliquots.
Write the volume and number of total cells on the vial label using a permanent marker or other identification method.
Place filled cryovials into controlled rate cryofreezing containers.
Store the controlled freezing container at −80°C for a minimum of four hours and a maximum of 96 hours before moving to cryoboxes.
Keep samples at −80°C for up to two weeks, then transfer to liquid nitrogen (LN2) for long-term storage.
